Hello, I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging the significant changes you've undergone recently, and I'm here to support you in any way I can. As part of our conversation today, I'll be using the EPDS to help us better understand your emotional well-being during this postpartum period. The EPDS is a tool that screens for depressive and anxiety symptoms, which can be common experiences for new mothers. It's essential to remember that this assessment is not about judging or diagnosing but rather about creating a safe space for you to express your feelings and concerns.

Please know that everything we discuss is confidential and respected. I'm here to listen and provide support without any judgment. The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help us understand your emotional state over the past 7 days. These questions are designed to be straightforward and easy to understand, and we'll take them one at a time. 

Let's get started. I want to begin by asking: Over the past 7 days, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

To be honest, it's been really tough for me to find the humor in things lately. I mean, I used to love watching comedies and laughing with my friends, but now it just feels like everything is so overwhelming. Taking care of the baby is a 24/7 job, and I'm just so tired all the time. I feel like I'm just going through the motions, you know? I'll be changing a diaper or feeding the baby, and my mind will just start wandering to all the things that could go wrong. It's hard to explain, but it's like my brain is always on high alert, waiting for something bad to happen. 

I do have moments where I'll see something cute the baby does, and I'll smile or even laugh for a second, but it's not like it used to be. It's like the laughter is just surface-level now, you know? It doesn't feel as genuine or as deep as it used to. And even when I do laugh, it's often followed by this wave of sadness or guilt, like I'm not doing enough or that I'm not a good enough mom. It's really confusing and exhausting. I just wish I could feel like myself again, you know?
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

No... I wouldn't say that's been me, unfortunately. Like I said, it's been hard to find the humor in things lately. I feel like I've lost touch with the things that used to make me happy, and even when I try to laugh or watch something funny, it just doesn't feel the same. It's like my mind is always preoccupied with worries about the baby's health, or if I'm doing everything right, or just feeling really overwhelmed and tired. It's hard to explain, but it's like my brain is just stuck in this anxious, worried mode, and it's hard to shake it off. Sometimes I'll see other moms laughing and joking, and it just makes me feel even more like I'm failing, you know? Like, why can't I be happy and carefree like they are? It's just really tough right now.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Honestly, not really. I used to love planning things and looking forward to them, but now it just feels like so much effort. Even things that I used to enjoy, like going for a walk or meeting up with friends, just seem like too much work now. I feel like I'm just trying to survive each day, rather than actually enjoying anything. And even when I do try to plan something, I just end up worrying about all the things that could go wrong, like the baby getting fussy or me not being able to get everything done that I need to. It's just hard to feel excited about anything when I'm feeling so overwhelmed and exhausted all the time.

I do try to look forward to little things, like my husband coming home from work or the baby smiling at me, but even those things can be fleeting. And sometimes, even when I do feel a little bit of happiness, it's quickly followed by feelings of guilt or anxiety, like I'm not doing enough or that something is going to go wrong. It's just really hard to enjoy anything right now, and it feels like I'm just going through the motions most of the time.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yes... that's definitely been me. I feel like I'm always blaming myself for something. If the baby is fussy, I think it's because I'm not feeding them right or I'm not changing their diaper often enough. If I'm tired, I think it's because I'm not managing my time well enough or I'm not prioritizing my own self-care. It's like I'm always looking for ways to criticize myself and feel like I'm not doing enough.

And it's not just the big things, it's the little things too. Like, if I forget to pack something in the diaper bag, I'll beat myself up over it and think that I'm a terrible mom. Or if I don't get a chance to shower for a few days, I'll feel like I'm disgusting and that the baby deserves better. It's like I'm always waiting for something to go wrong so I can pounce on it and say "see, I knew I wasn't good enough".

It's exhausting, to be honest. I feel like I'm always walking on eggshells, waiting for the other shoe to drop. And even when things do go right, I'll often think that it's just a fluke and that I'm just lucky. I don't feel like I'm ever really doing anything well, and that's a really hard feeling to shake.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Yes... that's been me a lot lately. I feel like I'm always worrying about something, even when everything seems fine. I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby or changing their diaper, and suddenly I'll start thinking about all the things that could go wrong. Like, what if the baby chokes on something? What if I forget to lock the door and someone breaks in? What if I'm not producing enough milk and the baby is starving?

It's like my brain is always racing with these worst-case scenarios, and it's hard to shut them off. Even when my husband tries to reassure me that everything is okay, I just can't seem to shake the feeling of anxiety. I'll be lying in bed at night, and my mind will start racing with all these fears and worries, and I'll feel my heart racing and my body tensing up.

It's not just about the baby, either. I'll worry about things like, what if I'm not a good enough mom? What if I'm not doing enough to support my husband? What if we're not financially stable enough to provide for the baby? It's like my brain is always looking for things to worry about, and it's exhausting.

Sometimes I'll try to distract myself by watching TV or scrolling through my phone, but even that doesn't always work. The worries just seem to linger in the back of my mind, waiting to pounce on me when I'm not expecting it. It's really hard to explain, but it's like I'm always waiting for something to go wrong, and that's a really anxious and scary feeling.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes... that's happened to me a few times. I'll be sitting there, doing something normal like feeding the baby or folding laundry, and suddenly I'll feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, my breath will get short, and I'll feel like I'm going to pass out. It's like my body is responding to some kind of threat, but there's no actual danger there.

It's really scary, because I don't know what's triggering it. Sometimes it happens when I'm alone with the baby, and I'll start thinking about all the things that could go wrong. Other times it happens when I'm in a crowded place, like the grocery store, and I'll feel overwhelmed by all the people and noise.

When it happens, I try to take some deep breaths and remind myself that everything is okay. I'll tell myself that I'm safe, that the baby is safe, and that I can handle whatever is happening. But it's hard to shake the feeling of panic, and it can take a while to calm down.

It's also really embarrassing, because sometimes I'll be in public when it happens, and I'll feel like everyone is staring at me. I'll try to hide it, but it's hard to pretend like everything is fine when I'm feeling so scared and overwhelmed.

I've also had some nights where I'll wake up in the middle of the night, feeling panicked and scared, and I won't be able to go back to sleep. I'll lie there, thinking about all the things that could go wrong, and feeling like I'm the only one who can protect the baby. It's a really isolating and frightening feeling, and it's hard to know how to make it stop.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes... that's definitely how I've been feeling. It's like everything is piling up on me, and I don't know how to keep up. Taking care of the baby is a 24/7 job, and it's exhausting. I feel like I'm always running on empty, and I don't have any energy left for anything else.

Even simple tasks, like laundry or dishes, feel like they're too much for me to handle. I'll look at the pile of dirty clothes or the stack of dirty dishes, and I'll just feel overwhelmed. I'll think to myself, "How am I going to get all of this done? I'm already so tired, and I don't have any energy left."

And it's not just the practical tasks. I feel like I'm also struggling to keep up with my own emotions. I'll have these moments where I'll feel okay, and then suddenly I'll be hit with a wave of sadness or anxiety. It's like I'm constantly trying to keep my head above water, but it's hard to stay afloat.

Sometimes I'll try to talk to my husband about how I'm feeling, but even that can be hard. I'll feel like I'm burdening him with my problems, and I don't want to add to his stress. So I'll just try to deal with it on my own, but that can be really isolating.

It's like I'm just trying to survive each day, rather than actually living. I feel like I'm just going through the motions, and I don't know how to break free from that. It's a really frustrating and overwhelming feeling, and it's hard to know how to make it stop.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes... that's been me lately. I've been having a really hard time sleeping, and it's not just because the baby is waking me up at night. Even when the baby is sleeping, I'll lie awake for hours, feeling anxious and overwhelmed. My mind will start racing, and I'll think about all the things that could go wrong, or all the things I need to do, and I just can't seem to calm down.

Sometimes I'll feel like I'm on the verge of tears, and I don't know why. It's like this deep sadness has settled inside of me, and I don't know how to shake it. I'll try to distract myself by watching TV or reading a book, but nothing seems to work. I'll just lie there, feeling miserable and alone, and wondering why I'm feeling this way.

It's not just at night, either. I'll feel unhappy and overwhelmed during the day, too. I'll be taking care of the baby, and I'll start to feel this sense of dread or anxiety. It's like I'm waiting for something to go wrong, and I don't know how to make it stop.

I've tried to talk to my husband about it, but even he doesn't seem to understand. He'll tell me to "just relax" or "try to get some rest," but it's not that easy. It's like my brain is wired to worry and stress, and I don't know how to turn it off.

I've also been having trouble falling asleep because I'm so worried about the baby. I'll lie awake, listening to the baby's monitor, and I'll worry that something is wrong. I'll get up and check on the baby, and then I'll lie back down and worry some more. It's like I'm trapped in this cycle of anxiety and worry, and I don't know how to escape.

It's really taking a toll on me, too. I feel like I'm running on empty, and I don't know how much longer I can keep going like this. I just wish I could find a way to calm down, and feel happy and relaxed again.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yes... that's been me a lot lately. I've been feeling really sad and miserable, and it's hard to explain why. I'll be taking care of the baby, and everything will seem fine, but then suddenly I'll just feel this wave of sadness wash over me. It's like I'm grieving for something, but I don't know what.

Sometimes it's triggered by little things, like a song or a smell that reminds me of before the baby was born. Other times it's just out of the blue, and I'll feel like I'm drowning in this sea of sadness. I'll try to talk to my husband about it, but even he doesn't seem to understand. He'll tell me that I'm a great mom, and that everything is okay, but it's hard to shake the feeling that something is wrong.

I've also been feeling really guilty about feeling this way. I mean, I'm supposed to be happy and grateful to have a healthy baby, right? But the truth is, I'm not feeling that way. I'm feeling overwhelmed and anxious, and I don't know how to make it stop.

It's hard to explain, but it's like I'm living in this fog of sadness and uncertainty. I'll have moments where I'll feel okay, but then the fog will roll back in, and I'll feel like I'm drowning again. It's really scary, and it's hard to know how to escape.

Sometimes I'll cry, and it's like the tears just won't stop. I'll feel like I'm sobbing for hours, and I don't know how to make it stop. It's like my body is just releasing all this pent-up emotion, and I don't know how to control it.

It's really hard to admit, but I've been feeling like I'm not a good mom. I feel like I'm failing the baby, and that I'm not doing enough. And that just makes the sadness and guilt worse. I feel like I'm trapped in this cycle of negative emotions, and I don't know how to break free.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yes... I've been crying a lot lately. It's like the tears just won't stop, and I don't know how to make them stop. I'll be taking care of the baby, and suddenly I'll just feel this overwhelming sadness, and I'll start crying. It's not just a little crying, either - it's like deep, sobbing crying that feels like it's coming from the depths of my soul.

Sometimes it's triggered by little things, like a commercial on TV or a song that reminds me of something. Other times it's just out of the blue, and I'll feel like I'm crying for no reason at all. But the truth is, I am crying for a reason - I'm crying because I'm feeling overwhelmed and anxious and scared, and I don't know how to make it stop.

I've been trying to hold it together, especially when my husband is around, but it's hard. I'll try to put on a brave face, but then I'll just start crying again. And it's not just when I'm alone, either - I've been crying in front of my husband, in front of my family, even in front of strangers. It's like I have no control over my emotions, and it's really scary.

The worst part is, I feel like I'm crying for things that don't even make sense. I'll be crying because I'm feeling guilty about something, or because I'm worried about the baby, or because I'm just feeling overwhelmed. And then I'll feel guilty for crying, because I'll think that I'm being weak or that I'm not a good mom.

It's like I'm trapped in this cycle of sadness and guilt, and I don't know how to escape. I just wish I could feel happy and carefree again, like I did before the baby was born. But right now, it feels like that's just a distant memory, and I'm not sure how to get back there.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

* Persistent feelings of sadness, loss of pleasure, and crying spells, indicating a potential low mood.
* Difficulty coping with daily responsibilities and feeling overwhelmed, suggesting struggles with anxiety and stress management.
* Sleep difficulties linked to mood, with reports of lying awake at night due to anxiety and worry.
* Feelings of worthlessness and guilt, particularly in relation to mothering and self-care.

* Loss of enjoyment in previously pleasurable activities and difficulty finding humor in things.
